chunks: From him, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from 'Is ibn al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the mutamatti' who arrives in Makkah on the Day of Tarwiyah at the time of salat al-'Asr: does the mut'ah pass him by? He said: No. He has the time between then and sunset.
And he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم had indeed done that.

key_terms.الْمُتْعَةُ: here, the Tamattu' rite of pilgrimage
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِ: sunset, the final time limit mentioned
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, a key day in the rites of hajj

ai.seo_question: Until what time can a pilgrim still catch Hajj al-Tamattu' if he reaches Makkah on the Day of Tarwiyah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a pilgrim performing Hajj al-Tamattu' who reaches Makkah on the Day of Tarwiyah at the time of salat al-'Asr has not yet missed the opportunity for mut'ah. The Imam عليه السلام sets the limit as extending until sunset and supports this by referring to the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
